topic: Humans Are Closer to T-Rex Than T-Rex Was to Stegosaurus

sentences.text: T. rex lived closer to your time than to Stegosaurus.
We picture them together, roaring at each other in one jungle.
But Stegosaurus was gone by about one hundred forty-five million years ago.
T. rex didn't show up until about sixty-nine million years ago.
That gap? Roughly seventy-six million years or more.
If T. rex could dig up fossils, Stegosaurus would've been one.
Now flip it. T. rex vanished about sixty-six million years ago.
And humans? We're brand new on that clock, a blink at the very end.
Walk back in time from today to the last T. rex.
Then keep walking that same distance again.
You still wouldn't reach a single Stegosaurus.

critic.critique: Sentences 3-5 stall the script with back-to-back date ranges in textbook tone. Cut them down to one punchy number per animal, and give sentence 6 a single round gap figure instead of a range. Sentence 9 never says how new humans are, so sentence 10 just repeats the hook. Give a concrete human figure or a vivid scale image, such as a clock or a football field, so the comparison lands as a felt shock. Emotional charge is flat: sentence 7 needs a more striking image, like T. rex being as far from Stegosaurus as we are from... something, to create awe rather than summary. Sentences 10 and 11 both start with "So"; merge them so the final line is a single sharp payoff that still runs straight into sentence 1 when the video loops.
